title: Astrid and the Extraction
premise: Paloma Lockridge, a veteran air-crash investigator, has spent twelve years chasing the truth about the accident that killed her family in row twelve — an investigation whose official findings keep shifting under her feet. When a stranger named Elias Vann repays a favor she never performed and claims he was on that flight but walked away, Paloma realizes the crash was staged to bury a secret her family carried: an inheritance of forged identities tied to a smuggling network inside the aviation authority. As the checkpoint schedules shift and hunters close in, Paloma must decide whether loyalty to the memory of her family matters more than the truth of who they really were. In the end she trades the secret — her own true identity as the network's intended heir — to expose the conspirators at the border crossing where it all began, walking through the checkpoint as someone new.
about_author: Ines Ishikawa is a former airline safety analyst who left the industry after a decade of near-misses she was never allowed to write up. She now writes thrillers from a coastal town where the fog arrives exactly on schedule.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the anniversary of the crash, Paloma re-reads the final report and notices the seating chart has been quietly amended — row twelve no longer exists in the records. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A stranger, Elias Vann, appears at Paloma's office claiming she once saved his life — a debt she has no memory of. He leaves a sealed envelope before vanishing. Emotional beat: uncanny disruption of a controlled life.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The envelope contains a boarding pass for flight 4471 — seat 12C — issued in her maiden name, dated the day of the crash. Someone expected her on that plane. Emotional beat: vertigo; her past rewrites itself.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She pulls archived maintenance logs and finds three versions of the same pre-flight inspection, each signed by a different inspector — one signature belongs to her father. Emotional beat: betrayal blooming inside mourning.

chapters.title: The Man Who Walked Away
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias tracks Paloma to explain: he was seated in row twelve, pulled off the flight minutes before departure by a man with authority credentials. He's been running for twelve years. Emotional beat: guilt and relief entangled.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Schedule
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following the paper trail, she learns the northern border checkpoint rotates its shift roster on a hidden cycle — and every rotation coincides with unlogged cargo flights. Emotional beat: pattern recognition as hope.

chapters.title: What Her Father Signed
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias reveals he recognized Paloma's father from the network: he wasn't a victim, he was a courier of forged identities, and Paloma herself may have been listed as an heir. Emotional beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: The Lockridge Ledger
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In her mother's belongings she finds a ledger of names — people who officially died in various accidents but appear alive elsewhere. Row twelve was a deletion list. Emotional beat: horror reframed as method.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over Her Shoulder
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias notices surveillance on Paloma's apartment and stages a break-in to make it look like the ledger was stolen, buying time. Emotional beat: protective instinct hardening into partnership.

chapters.title: The Inspector Who Didn't Drown
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She locates one name from the ledger alive: a former inspector living under a new identity, who confirms the network fakes deaths to move people — and that her father tried to exit. Emotional beat: reluctant witness, fragile truth.

chapters.title: Exit Fee
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The inspector is murdered hours after talking, staged as a heart attack. Elias realizes the network knows they're closing in. Emotional beat: fear converting urgency into resolve.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Audited
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Her supervisor — a mentor she trusted — offers her a promotion and a quiet warning to stop digging. She understands he's measuring her loyalty for the network. Emotional beat: loneliness of double consciousness.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Interest
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confesses his real role: he was the network's errand runner, and pulling him off the flight was punishment-adjacent mercy — the favor Paloma's father did for a stranger's son. Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: The Heir Clause
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Decoding the ledger, she finds her own name under an inheritance clause: control of the identity pipeline passes to her if claimed before a deadline — days away, timed to a checkpoint shift change. Emotional beat: trap disguised as birthright.

chapters.title: Shifting the Border
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. They map the shift-change window when the checkpoint runs skeleton staff and the network moves its ledger master across. Elias proposes they intercept it there. Emotional beat: plan crystallizing under pressure.

chapters.title: What Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma confronts what the secret actually is: not documents, but her own registered identity as the network's designated successor — the one thing both sides need her to claim or destroy. Emotional beat: the self as battlefield.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Confession
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The supervisor corners Elias, revealing he loved Paloma's mother and has been softening the network's hand for years. He gives them the shift-change code — then warns them someone higher will trade them both. Emotional beat: compromised ally, costly honesty.

chapters.title: Night of the Rotation
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the checkpoint, Paloma poses as a traveler while Elias infiltrates the freight lane. The ledger master arrives early; the plan frays as scanners flag her altered ID. Emotional beat: terror held behind a calm face.

chapters.title: Trade
chapters.summary: Both POVs interleaved. Cornered between the network's enforcer and the checkpoint cameras, Paloma offers the trade: the heir claim in exchange for the ledger master and live exposure of the conspiracy. Elias triggers the dead-drop broadcast. Emotional beat: sacrifice as leverage.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The broadcast forces the incoming shift to act; enforcers scatter, the ledger master is seized, and the supervisor takes a bullet shielding Paloma. Emotional beat: chaos resolving into terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Name She Trades
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. In the aftermath, Paloma formally renounces the inheritance, dissolving the network's legal spine — but the renunciation requires surrendering the Lockridge name itself into the record. Emotional beat: freedom priced in identity.

chapters.title: Astrid
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Weeks later, a woman with new papers walks through the border checkpoint under a name chosen from her mother's ledger — Astrid — while Elias waits on the other side. She finally visits a grave marked row twelve. Emotional beat: grief integrated; identity chosen, not inherited.
